title: Evaluation of proteins such as α-synuclein in lymph nodes of patients with and without confirmed neurodegenerative disease and their predictive value for the early detection of neurodegenerative diseases.
summary:
Parkinson's disease is a progressive disorder of the nervous system. In addition to movement disorders, non-motor symptoms—such as sleep disturbances, depressive symptoms, or a reduced sense of smell—can also occur. The protein alpha-synuclein plays a key role in this process; in Parkinson's disease, it undergoes changes and can accumulate in tissues.

There is growing evidence that the disease affects not only the brain but also other parts of the body. Consequently, this study compares lymph nodes from patients with Parkinson's disease with those from individuals who do not have a known neurodegenerative disorder. Both lymph nodes containing tumors and those free of tumors are being examined.

The aim is to determine whether alpha-synuclein can be detected in lymph nodes and whether there are differences between the groups under study.
conditions: Other degenerative diseases of nervous system, not elsewhere classified
